newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS-Italy car sector booms, incentives may go on.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Italy car sector booms, incentives may go on.

text.p: Italy's car market, boosted by the success of a scheme to encourage drivers to trade in their old vehicles and buy new ones, surged further in June when new registrations rose more than 50 percent compared with last year.

Transport Minister Claudio Burlando told reporters in Turin on Wednesday that new car registrations were up 50.71 percent to 222,800 units in the month while registrations in the first half of 1997 were up nearly one third on last year at 1,312,400.
Because of the car boom, ministers indicated they were reluctant to slam the brakes on the incentives scheme, which has exceeded expectations since it was launched in January.
The scheme had been due to end in September.
"The government is discussing (an extension) and things are at an advanced stage," Environment Minister Edo Ronchi told reporters in Rome.
"The incentives scheme has had far better results than we expected. Nonetheless, there's still significant demand out there to satisfy," he said.

In the first six months of the scheme, which allows Italians to obtain discounts if they swap cars which have been on the road for more than 10 years for new ones, 444,744 vehicles were cancelled from the national car register and 348,805 new cars were registered.

The scheme has cost the government more than 570 billion lire ($332 million) in payouts, while dealers have offered discounts worth 800 billion lire, but carmakers say the huge surge in new registrations means the Treasury has actually made money in increased fiscal revenue.

Burlando, who has said recently that the government was studying "an intelligent exit" from the scheme, told Italian car makers' association ANFIA on Wednesday that it was keen "to avoid abrupt downscaling" by scrapping the incentives suddenly.
Fiat chairman Cesare Romiti has warned against the dangers to the car industry of a sudden end to the incentives.

Fiat's own new registrations were 65 percent higher in June at 102,100, transport ministry data showed. Fiat is Italy's biggest carmaker and comprises the marques Fiat, Alfa Romeo, Lancia Autobianchi, and Fiat-Innocenti. ($1=1,716 lire)
